15: # Rule Anatomy Contract
16: 
17: Derived from the corpus under `.skilled/repo-rules/` plus the router, parsed structurally rather
18: than recalled. Nothing below is aspirational: every MUST element is carried by every
19: shipped rule.
20: 
21: Corpus figures are deliberately not restated here. To see the current ones, run
22: `node .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-repo-rule/scripts/check-repo-rules.cjs` (the
23: corpus checker) from the repository root. Its eleven checks report count parity, link wiring,
24: trigger-phrase uniqueness, the line ceiling, frontmatter keys, divider parity, rule-body
25: links, fires-when sections, index summaries against each rule's description,
26: fires-when coverage (every Fires-when bullet named in its router row), and card sync
27: (every committed card under `cards/` equal to the card `build-rule-cards.cjs` renders from
28: its rule) for the corpus as it stands.
29: 
30: ---
31: 
32: ## 1. OVERVIEW: WHAT A REPO RULE IS
33: 
34: A repo rule **supplements the harness**. It is not a law and not a contract with the
35: runtime: it can be overridden by an explicit operator instruction, changed when it stops
36: matching how the work is actually done, and removed when it stops earning its load.
37: 
38: Three consequences the template must carry:
39: 
40: - **A rule sits below `AGENTS.md` and below a live operator instruction.** Every shipped
41:   rule says so in its own header line, verbatim, without exception. That line is not
42:   boilerplate to be trimmed — it is the rule declaring its own rank.
43: - **A rule is revisable.** It carries a `version` field for exactly this reason. Writing
44:   one is not a permanent commitment, and treating it as one is what produces rules nobody
45:   will delete after they stop being true.
46: - **Removal is a normal outcome.** The set has already subtracted once — a duplicated
47:   restraint ladder whose rung numbering contradicted the authoritative one. A review that
48:   only ever adds has not reviewed anything.
49: 
50: This is why the mode owns changing and removing rules, not only creating them.
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## 2. WHAT THE CORPUS AGREES ON
55: 
56: Every one of these is carried by every shipped rule. A generated rule that omits any is not a rule of this set.
57: 
58: | Element | Shape | Evidence |
59: |---------|-------|----------|
60: | Frontmatter | Six keys, one order: `title`, `description`, `trigger_phrases`, `importance_tier`, `contextType`, `version` | Every rule, in exactly one distinct key order across the corpus |
61: | Title line | `# Rule: <Subject>` | Every rule |
62: | Routed-from line | `> Routed from [REPO RULES.md](../../REPO%20RULES.md). <when to load>.` under `.skilled/repo-rules/`, or `../REPO%20RULES.md` under a root `repo-rules/` | Every rule |
63: | Subordination line | `> Expands AGENTS.md, never overrides it. Where they appear to disagree, AGENTS.md wins and this file is wrong. Say so.` | Every rule, verbatim |
64: | `## Fires when` | Unnumbered; a bullet list of actions, not topics | Every rule |
65: | `## The rule` | Unnumbered; exactly one bold binding sentence, then at most a short gloss | Every rule |
66: | Numbered body | `## N. ALL CAPS TITLE`, sequential from 1 | Every rule, all uppercase outside backticks |
67: | Divider discipline | One `---` per numbered section | Every rule and the router — dividers equal numbered sections, with no exception |
68: | Closing self-check | Final numbered section, titled `SELF-CHECK`, a `- [ ]` checklist | Every rule |
69: | Back-link | A link to the router that resolves from the rule's own folder: `../../REPO%20RULES.md` from `.skilled/repo-rules/`, `../REPO%20RULES.md` from a root `repo-rules/` | Every rule |
70: 
71: **The strongest invariant is the divider rule.** Dividers equal numbered sections in
72: every file including the router, with zero variance. It is the one structural property a
73: generator can assert without qualification.
74: 
75: ---
76: 
77: ## 3. WHAT VARIES, AND WHY
78: 
79: These scale with the rule's subject. A generator sets no target for them.
80: 
81: | Element | What varies, and why |
82: |---------|----------------------|
83: | `trigger_phrases` | Find surface, not an index: a rule with more distinct symptoms earns more phrases |
84: | Numbered sections | Follows the subject — a rule that turns on more distinct mechanisms carries more sections |
85: | Self-check items | One per obligation the body actually creates |
86: | Total lines | Follows section count, which follows the subject |
87: | Inter-rule cross-references | Sparse; rules are more independent than the cross-reference doctrine implies. See section 5 |
88: | Example-and-repair line | Optional: the tempting wrong move beside its repair, earned when the rule names a habit. The template carries it and the shipped corpus predates it |
89: 
90: ---
91: 
92: ## 4. LENGTH BANDS
93: 
94: Operator-set, and they replace the stale ~160 ceiling the set carried before these
95: bands. Counts include frontmatter, because that is what a reader loads.
96: 
97: | Band | Range | Meaning |
98: |------|-------|---------|
99: | **Preferred** | ≤ 160 | Where a rule should land. Most subjects fit |
100: | **Good** | 161-200 | Acceptable without comment |
101: | **At the limit** | 201-250 | Allowed, but the rule should be able to say why it needs the room |
102: | **Over** | > 250 | Split it, or cut it |
103: 
104: The **Over** band is also enforced mechanically: the corpus checker treats any rule over
105: 250 as a failure.
106: 
107: A rule at the limit should be able to say why it needs the room — content moved down
108: from `AGENTS.md` is a sufficient reason. A new rule that reaches the limit with no such
109: explanation should be looked at.
110: 
111: > A band is checkable, which the proportionality rule this replaces was not. That
112: > trade was deliberate: an enforceable approximation beats an unenforceable truth.
113: 
114: ---
115: 
116: ## 5. A SECOND FINDING: THE RULES ARE NEARLY INDEPENDENT
117: 
118: Every rule links back to the router, and sideways links between rules stay few next to
119: the doctrine each rule holds. `check-repo-rules.cjs` reports the live link count, so this
120: page states no number that can go stale.
121: 
122: "Cross-reference rather than restate" was written as a duplication guard, and the
123: outcome is that rules rarely need each other. A generated rule should therefore default to
124: **zero** sideways links, and add one only where it would otherwise restate another rule's
125: doctrine.
126: 
127: ---
128: 
129: ## 6. THE FRONTMATTER SCHEMA
130: 
131: Six keys, in this order, matching the skill-reference schema:
132: 
133: ```yaml
134: ---
135: title: "Rule: <Subject>"
136: description: "<one sentence: the binding rule, restated for a reader who will not open the file>"
137: trigger_phrases:
138:   - "<the words someone reaches for when they have the problem>"
139: importance_tier: important
140: contextType: reference
141: version: 1.0.0.0
142: ---
143: ```
144: 
145: **`title` and `description` MUST be quoted.** Both routinely contain a colon — `title`
146: always does, because the convention is `Rule: <Subject>`. Unquoted, the block is invalid
147: YAML. Files have failed to parse on first authoring for exactly this reason, and the
148: failure is invisible to a reader: it looks correct and only a parser objects.
149: 
150: **`trigger_phrases` carry symptom vocabulary, not section titles.** The section titles are
151: already greppable from the body; the phrases exist to catch someone who has the problem
152: and does not know the rule's name. The corpus checker enforces uniqueness: no phrase is
153: claimed by two rules, so each phrase resolves to exactly one file.
154: 
155: ---
156: 
157: ## 7. SECTION ORDER
158: 
159: The body order is not arbitrary and is consistent where subjects overlap:
160: 
161: 1. The mechanism or scale the rule turns on — the ladder, the tiers, the registers.
162: 2. How to apply it, in the order a reader hits the decisions.
163: 3. Composition with other rules, where any exists.
164: 4. `WHAT THIS RULE IS NOT` — where present, it was added after a misreading occurred.
165:    Recommended whenever a rule could be read as licence.
166: 5. `SELF-CHECK` — always last, one item per obligation the body creates.
167: 
168: ---
169: 
170: ## 8. SELF-CHECK
171: 
172: - [ ] Every MUST element in section 2 appears in the generated rule.
173: - [ ] Dividers equal numbered sections exactly.
174: - [ ] `title` and `description` are quoted, and the frontmatter parses.
175: - [ ] Trigger phrases are symptom vocabulary, and none duplicates another rule's.
176: - [ ] Every numbered section names a failure it prevents.
177: - [ ] Self-check items correspond one-to-one with the obligations the body creates.
178: - [ ] Sideways cross-references default to zero; any that exist replace a restatement.
179: - [ ] Length lands in a band, and a rule at the limit can say why it needs the room.
180: - [ ] The header line declaring the rule's rank below `AGENTS.md` is present, verbatim.

1: ---
2: title: "Decision Tests: May This Rule Exist?"
3: description: "Four tests recovered from the phases that established them, deciding whether a proposed repo rule may exist at all and where its content belongs if it may not. Reproduces the ten refusals the rule set already made."
4: trigger_phrases:
5:   - "may this rule exist"
6:   - "always-loaded versus triggered"
7:   - "router scope boundary"
8:   - "rule refusal test"
9:   - "where does this content belong"
10: importance_tier: important
11: contextType: reference
12: version: 1.1.1.0
13: ---
14: 
15: # Decision Tests: May This Rule Exist?
16: 
17: Run these before writing anything. They decide **whether** a rule may exist, which is a
18: different question from how it should read — `rule-anatomy.md` answers that one, and only
19: matters once these four pass.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 1. OVERVIEW
24: 
25: Each test is recovered from the phase record that established it, not restated from
26: memory.
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ## 2. THE ALWAYS-LOADED TEST
31: 
32: > **A rule file loads on a trigger. Content that must bind when no trigger has fired
33: > cannot live in one.**
34: 
35: This is the test that decides most refusals, and it is the least intuitive, because a
36: rule can be correct, well-written, and still belong somewhere else entirely.
37: 
38: **Ask:** on a turn where nothing fires, must this still hold?
39: 
40: - **Yes** → it belongs in `AGENTS.md`. Refuse the rule.
41: - **No** → continue to test 2.
42: 
43: **Recovered from:** the research phase found 18 row-groups in `AGENTS.md` that could not
44: move down, and they "reduce to one property: always-loaded force." The adoption phase
45: applied it to refuse relocating Violation Recovery, whose trigger fires exactly when the
46: trigger-loaded path may already be broken.
47: 
48: **The instructive near-miss:** the communication rule moved almost entirely out of
49: `AGENTS.md` §8 anyway, on an operator decision. It survives only because its trigger was
50: widened to *every substantive reply* — and §8 still keeps the two clauses that must bind
51: unconditionally. A total move needs a total trigger, or the content goes quiet.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## 3. THE SCOPE BOUNDARY TEST
56: 
57: > **The router states what the rule set is In and Out for. Out is not advisory.**
58: 
59: **In:** how to think and act — restraint, scope, evidence, risk, diagnosis, honesty, the
60: posture when work is handed to another runtime, and how the resulting reply reads.
61: 
62: **Out:** skill routing, workflow selection, spec-folder mechanics, and the *mechanics* of
63: agent and CLI dispatch — which agent, which command, which model, which flags.
64: 
65: **Ask:** is the proposal routing, or is it posture?
66: 
67: - **Routing** → refuse. `AGENTS.md` §2 and the skills it routes to own it.
68: - **Posture** → continue to test 3.
69: 
70: **The line:** *how to dispatch is theirs; how to think while dispatching is ours.*
71: 
72: **Recovered from:** the router's own section 4, which has been widened exactly four
73: times and every time deliberately — to admit delegation posture, then delivery, then a
74: narrow routing carve-out, then the ask-surface carve-out. The third is the instructive
75: one: it admits *verifying wiring you changed* as an evidence obligation, and still
76: refuses *selecting* a route. A fifth widening that admitted selection would dissolve
77: the boundary the set exists to hold.
78: 
79: **So the test did not get weaker.** Ask which side of the carve-out the proposal sits on.
80: A rule about which skill, command, model or flags to pick is still refused here.
81: 
82: ---
83: 
84: ## 4. THE FOUR-PART REFUSAL TEST
85: 
86: A proposal must pass **all four** to become a rule file.
87: 
88: | # | Condition | Fails when |
89: |---|-----------|-----------|
90: | 1 | It is a **trigger-shaped cluster** | It is a single row, not a cluster. One row is a section in an existing rule |
91: | 2 | It has **no existing home** | Another rule already carries it, and the proposal is duplication |
92: | 3 | It is **not design-excluded** | Test 2 already refused it |
93: | 4 | It has an **`AGENTS.md` anchor** | Nothing in the always-loaded document points at it, so nothing would ever load it |
94: 
95: **Recovered from:** the adoption phase used exactly this to refuse ten candidates —
96: gate-discipline, git/PR, communication-format, testing, security, memory, spec-folder,
97: skill-routing, delegation-mechanics, and collaboration.
98: 
99: **Reproduction check.** These four must still refuse all ten, for the same reasons. If a
100: candidate now passes, either the test has drifted or the set has changed and the change
101: must be deliberate.
102: 
103: ---
104: 
105: ## 5. THE RESTRAINT TEST
106: 
107: > **The rule set is subject to its own `overengineering.md`.**
108: 
109: A set that grows because more rules feel thorough has failed the rule it ships.
110: 
111: **Ask:** what fails today without this rule?
112: 
113: - **Nothing concrete** → refuse. "Might need it", "best practice", and "for completeness"
114:   are the vocabulary that rule guards against.
115: - **A named failure** → the proposal is admissible; write it.
116: 
117: **Recovered from:** the research phase returned zero new rule files across five
118: iterations, and its single most valuable output was a **subtraction** — a duplicated
119: restraint ladder whose rung numbering contradicted the authoritative one.
120: 
121: **A review of a rule set that only adds has not reviewed it.**
122: 
123: ---
124: 
125: ## 6. WHERE IT GOES IF IT IS NOT A RULE
126: 
127: Refusing is not the end of the decision. Every refusal routes somewhere:
128: 
129: | Refused by | Belongs in |
130: |------------|-----------|
131: | Test 1, always-loaded | `AGENTS.md`, as a compressed row |
132: | Test 2, routing | `AGENTS.md` §2, or the skill its router resolves |
133: | Test 3 part 2, has a home | A new section inside the rule that already owns it |
134: | Test 3 part 1, single row | A section, not a file |
135: | Test 4, restraint | Nowhere. Record the refusal with its reason so it is not re-proposed |
136: 
137: **Record every refusal with the test it failed.** A declined proposal with a written
138: reason is what stops the same suggestion arriving next quarter with nobody remembering
139: why it was refused.
140: 
141: **Where the record lives:** the decision record of the spec packet that owns the rule
142: set for that repository. Spec folders are where this repository keeps refusal history,
143: diffed and archived with the work, and the rule files and the router stay free of it.
144: 
145: ---
146: 
147: ## 7. SELF-CHECK
148: 
149: - [ ] The proposal was tested against all four gates, in order, before any drafting.
150: - [ ] Test 1 was answered by asking what happens on a turn where nothing fires.
151: - [ ] The scope boundary was quoted, not paraphrased, when it decided a refusal.
152: - [ ] The four-part test still refuses the ten candidates the set already declined.
153: - [ ] The restraint test was answered with a failure that happens today.
154: - [ ] A refusal names the test it failed and where the content goes instead.

15: # Decision Tests: May This Rule Exist?
16: 
17: Run these before writing anything. They decide **whether** a rule may exist, which is a
18: different question from how it should read — `rule-anatomy.md` answers that one, and only
19: matters once these four pass.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 1. OVERVIEW
24: 
25: Each test is recovered from the phase record that established it, not restated from
26: memory.
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ## 2. THE ALWAYS-LOADED TEST
31: 
32: > **A rule file loads on a trigger. Content that must bind when no trigger has fired
33: > cannot live in one.**
34: 
35: This is the test that decides most refusals, and it is the least intuitive, because a
36: rule can be correct, well-written, and still belong somewhere else entirely.
37: 
38: **Ask:** on a turn where nothing fires, must this still hold?
39: 
40: - **Yes** → it belongs in `AGENTS.md`. Refuse the rule.
41: - **No** → continue to test 2.
42: 
43: **Recovered from:** the research phase found 18 row-groups in `AGENTS.md` that could not
44: move down, and they "reduce to one property: always-loaded force." The adoption phase
45: applied it to refuse relocating Violation Recovery, whose trigger fires exactly when the
46: trigger-loaded path may already be broken.
47: 
48: **The instructive near-miss:** the communication rule moved almost entirely out of
49: `AGENTS.md` §8 anyway, on an operator decision. It survives only because its trigger was
50: widened to *every substantive reply* — and §8 still keeps the two clauses that must bind
51: unconditionally. A total move needs a total trigger, or the content goes quiet.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## 3. THE SCOPE BOUNDARY TEST
56: 
57: > **The router states what the rule set is In and Out for. Out is not advisory.**
58: 
59: **In:** how to think and act — restraint, scope, evidence, risk, diagnosis, honesty, the
60: posture when work is handed to another runtime, and how the resulting reply reads.
61: 
62: **Out:** skill routing, workflow selection, spec-folder mechanics, and the *mechanics* of
63: agent and CLI dispatch — which agent, which command, which model, which flags.
64: 
65: **Ask:** is the proposal routing, or is it posture?
66: 
67: - **Routing** → refuse. `AGENTS.md` §2 and the skills it routes to own it.
68: - **Posture** → continue to test 3.
69: 
70: **The line:** *how to dispatch is theirs; how to think while dispatching is ours.*
71: 
72: **Recovered from:** the router's own section 4, which has been widened exactly four
73: times and every time deliberately — to admit delegation posture, then delivery, then a
74: narrow routing carve-out, then the ask-surface carve-out. The third is the instructive
75: one: it admits *verifying wiring you changed* as an evidence obligation, and still
76: refuses *selecting* a route. A fifth widening that admitted selection would dissolve
77: the boundary the set exists to hold.
78: 
79: **So the test did not get weaker.** Ask which side of the carve-out the proposal sits on.
80: A rule about which skill, command, model or flags to pick is still refused here.
81: 
82: ---
83: 
84: ## 4. THE FOUR-PART REFUSAL TEST
85: 
86: A proposal must pass **all four** to become a rule file.
87: 
88: | # | Condition | Fails when |
89: |---|-----------|-----------|
90: | 1 | It is a **trigger-shaped cluster** | It is a single row, not a cluster. One row is a section in an existing rule |
91: | 2 | It has **no existing home** | Another rule already carries it, and the proposal is duplication |
92: | 3 | It is **not design-excluded** | Test 2 already refused it |
93: | 4 | It has an **`AGENTS.md` anchor** | Nothing in the always-loaded document points at it, so nothing would ever load it |
94: 
95: **Recovered from:** the adoption phase used exactly this to refuse ten candidates —
96: gate-discipline, git/PR, communication-format, testing, security, memory, spec-folder,
97: skill-routing, delegation-mechanics, and collaboration.
98: 
99: **Reproduction check.** These four must still refuse all ten, for the same reasons. If a
100: candidate now passes, either the test has drifted or the set has changed and the change
101: must be deliberate.
102: 
103: ---
104: 
105: ## 5. THE RESTRAINT TEST
106: 
107: > **The rule set is subject to its own `overengineering.md`.**
108: 
109: A set that grows because more rules feel thorough has failed the rule it ships.
110: 
111: **Ask:** what fails today without this rule?
112: 
113: - **Nothing concrete** → refuse. "Might need it", "best practice", and "for completeness"
114:   are the vocabulary that rule guards against.
115: - **A named failure** → the proposal is admissible; write it.
116: 
117: **Recovered from:** the research phase returned zero new rule files across five
118: iterations, and its single most valuable output was a **subtraction** — a duplicated
119: restraint ladder whose rung numbering contradicted the authoritative one.
120: 
121: **A review of a rule set that only adds has not reviewed it.**
122: 
123: ---
124: 
125: ## 6. WHERE IT GOES IF IT IS NOT A RULE
126: 
127: Refusing is not the end of the decision. Every refusal routes somewhere:
128: 
129: | Refused by | Belongs in |
130: |------------|-----------|
131: | Test 1, always-loaded | `AGENTS.md`, as a compressed row |
132: | Test 2, routing | `AGENTS.md` §2, or the skill its router resolves |
133: | Test 3 part 2, has a home | A new section inside the rule that already owns it |
134: | Test 3 part 1, single row | A section, not a file |
135: | Test 4, restraint | Nowhere. Record the refusal with its reason so it is not re-proposed |
136: 
137: **Record every refusal with the test it failed.** A declined proposal with a written
138: reason is what stops the same suggestion arriving next quarter with nobody remembering
139: why it was refused.
140: 
141: **Where the record lives:** the decision record of the spec packet that owns the rule
142: set for that repository. Spec folders are where this repository keeps refusal history,
143: diffed and archived with the work, and the rule files and the router stay free of it.
144: 
145: ---
146: 
147: ## 7. SELF-CHECK
148: 
149: - [ ] The proposal was tested against all four gates, in order, before any drafting.
150: - [ ] Test 1 was answered by asking what happens on a turn where nothing fires.
151: - [ ] The scope boundary was quoted, not paraphrased, when it decided a refusal.
152: - [ ] The four-part test still refuses the ten candidates the set already declined.
153: - [ ] The restraint test was answered with a failure that happens today.
154: - [ ] A refusal names the test it failed and where the content goes instead.

681: 
682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868:

884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006:

1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

79: ## 4. SCOPE OF THIS DOCUMENT
80: 
81: **In:** how to think and act, restraint, scope, evidence, risk, diagnosis, honesty,
82: the posture to hold when work is handed to another runtime, how the resulting reply
83: reads, what you may claim about wiring you have changed, and how a turn hands control
84: back to the operator. The delegation posture was the first widening and Delivery the
85: second, added when `AGENTS.md` §8 moved down. Delivery is one of two rules here whose
86: trigger is a whole turn rather than a specific action, the other being the handback rule,
87: which fires at every turn's end, and `AGENTS.md` §4, under Reply Rules and Mandates, keeps
88: the two clauses that must bind even when nothing loads.
89: 
90: **Out:** skill routing, workflow selection, spec-folder mechanics, and the *mechanics*
91: of agent and CLI dispatch: which agent, which command, which model, which flags.
92: Those belong to `AGENTS.md` §2 and the skills it routes to, and are deliberately
93: absent here so each has exactly one place to change. The line is between plumbing and
94: posture: how to dispatch is theirs, how to think while dispatching is ours.
95: 
96: **The routing carve-out, added deliberately as the third widening.** *Selecting* a
97: route stays Out. *Verifying wiring you changed, and what you may claim about it*, is
98: In; it is an evidence obligation whose subject happens to be routing. `skill-hub-routing.md`
99: is the one rule on this side of that line, and it carries no route-selection guidance:
100: the mechanics stay in the skills, and the rule points at them. A fourth widening that
101: admits selection itself would dissolve the boundary; this one does not.
102: 
103: **The ask-surface carve-out, added as the fourth widening, on an operator decision that
104: overrode a research refusal.** A four-iteration decision-test run returned *refuse* here:
105: naming a question tool per runtime reads as the "which command" family, and the paragraph
106: above pre-refuses a fourth widening that admits selection. The operator widened it anyway,
107: and what follows is the narrowing that keeps the boundary standing. *Choosing between
108: runtimes, agents, commands, models or flags* stays Out, unchanged. *Naming the surface that
109: asks the operator a question, in the runtime you are already running in*, is In. That is not
110: a selection, because nothing is being selected: the runtime is a given, and the rule records
111: which of its surfaces carries an obligation the rule already imposes. `communication-handoff.md`
112: is the one rule on this side of that line, its §5 is the only place a tool name appears, and
113: it names only what this repository confirms. A fifth widening that let a rule pick between
114: runtimes would be the dissolution this one avoids.
